name: Ulvestad Variation — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Ulvestad Variation. Find the winning 2-move sequence to exploit the active Black knights and seize the initiative.

drills.name: c3 Attack on Nd4
drills.description: White attacks the knight on d4.
drills.briefExplanation: c3 attacks the knight on d4. If Black doesn't recapture the pawn immediately, White wins the knight.
drills.explanation: cxd4 wins the knight. White continues with 9.Qa4+ and 10.Qxd4, winning material. The c3 advance threatens the centralized knight immediately — Black must act or lose material on d4.

drills.name: Ne4 Central Outpost
drills.description: White plants the knight in the center.
drills.briefExplanation: Ne4 plants the knight in the center. After c6, d3 supports the knight and prepares Bg5.
drills.explanation: d3 supports the knight. White follows with 10.Bg5, pinning and attacking. The Ne4 outpost combined with the d3 support gives White a stable center and the initiative to press forward with Bg5 and a lasting bind.

drills.name: Qa4+ Check
drills.description: White checks the king and wins the knight.
drills.briefExplanation: Qa4+ checks the king immediately. When the king moves, White wins the knight on d4.
drills.explanation: Qxd4 wins the knight. White continues with 10.d3, consolidating. The queen check forces the king into the open — with the king misplaced on e7, White wins material while maintaining the initiative in the sharp Ulvestad position.

drills.name: Bg5 Pin
drills.description: White pins the knight on f6.
drills.briefExplanation: Bg5 pins the knight on f6 against the queen. Even after h6, White takes the knight anyway.
drills.explanation: Bxf6 damages Black's structure. White follows with 11.Qa4+, winning material. The bishop sacrifice is worth it — after Bxf6 gxf6, Black's kingside pawns are wrecked and White has a powerful initiative in the open position.
